s1.syndrome_frame: Facial asymmetry with possible cranial nerve involvement in a neonate
salient_findings: Enhancing mass in the left cerebellopontine angle and internal auditory canal on MRI
Profound hearing loss in the left ear on auditory brainstem response testing
key_facts: 4-week-old male patient
Left facial asymmetry observed during crying
Passed infant hearing screening previously
MRI showed an enhancing mass in the left cerebellopontine angle and internal auditory canal
Follow-up MRI showed considerable growth of the mass
Auditory brainstem response testing demonstrated profound hearing loss in the left ear
Histopathological examination revealed a vascular lesion with low levels of mitotic activity
Biphasic lesion composed of vascular nodules among spindle cells
Ki-67 labeling index: 5% to 10%
CD34 and CD31: Positive for endothelial cells

raw.syndrome_frame: Facial asymmetry with possible cranial nerve involvement in a neonate
salient_findings: Enhancing mass in the left cerebellopontine angle and internal auditory canal on MRI
Profound hearing loss in the left ear on auditory brainstem response testing

MRI showed an enhancing mass in the left cerebellopontine angle and internal auditory canal
Follow-up MRI showed considerable growth of the mass
Auditory brainstem response testing demonstrated profound hearing loss in the left ear
Histopathological examination revealed a vascular lesion with low levels of mitotic activity

Ki-67 labeling index: 5% to 10%
CD34 and CD31: Positive for endothelial cells

raw.rationale: The patient's MRI showed an enhancing mass in the left cerebellopontine angle and internal auditory canal with considerable growth on follow-up, and histopathological examination revealed a vascular lesion with low levels of mitotic activity and a biphasic pattern, which is consistent with hemangioma.

rejected.label: Cavernous Hemangioma
rejected.why: Cavernous hemangiomas are typically characterized by large, cavernous spaces and are less likely to show significant growth on follow-up imaging.

rejected.label: Vestibular Schwannoma
rejected.why: Vestibular schwannomas are typically slow-growing and are more common in adults, and the histopathological findings do not match.

rejected.label: Schwannoma
rejected.why: Schwannomas are typically composed of spindle cells, but the presence of vascular nodules and a biphasic pattern is not characteristic.

rejected.label: Lymphangioma
rejected.why: While the histopathological findings mention a pattern similar to lymphangiomatosis, the presence of CD34 and CD31 positivity and the overall clinical presentation are more consistent with hemangioma.
